nodes.label: GTM Container GTM-MRM597NW
nodes.rationale: Zero-code tag management: all GA4 event tags, click triggers and the Google Ads conversion live in GTM (v3 tags, container v4/v5) rather than in site code, so Romain's measurement can evolve without redeploying the site.

nodes.label: GA4 Property G-99EMNQYCK1
nodes.rationale: Only public identifier deliberately kept in this public repo (present in every page's HTML by construction); account IDs are kept out to limit targeted phishing. A 503 on collect from Antonin's Chrome is a local blocker artifact, not a site bug: curl returns 204.

nodes.label: Consent Mode v2
nodes.rationale: Initialized to granted unless localStorage.rb_cookies_v3 == 'min'. The inline block MUST stay before the GTM snippet in the <head> of all 3 pages, otherwise GA4 sends a page_view before a refusal is applied. The 3 blocks are identical, verified by md5.

nodes.label: Opt-out Consent Rule (no response = acceptance)
nodes.rationale: Antonin's deliberate decision: absence of response counts as acceptance; only an explicit refusal cuts measurement, immediately and on later visits. CNIL in principle requires prior consent, so real regulatory exposure is knowingly assumed (audit 24/07). Known limits: banner only on the public page, first page_view fires before any refusal, numbers are a floor, admin browsing is included. A strict rollback path (all signals denied by default + wait_for_update) is documented.

nodes.label: rb_cookies_v3 Consent Key
nodes.rationale: The localStorage key increments with each new consent purpose: rb_cookies (technical only), _v2 (audience measurement, 21/07), _v3 (Google Ads conversion, 24/07). Without the key bump, returning visitors would be measured for a purpose no banner ever declared to them. Any new purpose requires incrementing the key and updating banner + cookie policy.

nodes.label: demande_reservation Event
nodes.source_location: section 2. Les événements envoyés par le code
nodes.rationale: Pushed to dataLayer only AFTER the DB write, so a request refused for unavailable dates never counts; carries vehicule/forfait/nb_nuits, no personal data. Measurement hole fixed 2026-08-04 (commit 7ad6d87): from 21/07 to 04/08 only /app pushed the event, so public-form requests — exactly where Google Ads traffic lands — were counted nowhere; pre-04/08 request counts are undervalued. Test events (vehicule=test, 21-22/07 and 05/08) are filtered from all counters.

nodes.label: section_vue Event
nodes.rationale: One push per section per page load, values vans/penelop/peggy/tente/conception/apropos/faq/contact/devis. Vehicle slugs are aligned with the reservation slugs (penelop without final e) so views and conversions can be cross-tabulated per vehicle in GA4 without remapping.

nodes.label: GTM Click Triggers (tel / mailto / WhatsApp / Instagram)
nodes.rationale: Indispensable because GA4 enhanced measurement does not treat tel: and mailto: as outbound clicks, so it would never count them on its own. Four link-click triggers on Click URL mapped to clic_telephone, clic_email, clic_whatsapp, clic_instagram.
nodes.norm_label: gtm click triggers (tel / mailto / whatsapp / instagram)

nodes.label: GTM Data Layer Variables (vehicule, forfait, nb_nuits, section)
nodes.rationale: Without these DLVs the parameters pushed by the site never reach GA4 and the custom dimensions stay empty — GTM does not read dataLayer keys on its own; they are referenced as {{DLV - vehicule}} etc. in the event tags' parameters.
nodes.norm_label: gtm data layer variables (vehicule, forfait, nb_nuits, section)

nodes.label: GA4 Custom Dimensions (Section, Vehicule, Forfait)
nodes.rationale: Event-scoped custom definitions; NOT retroactive — they only collect from creation onward, which is why they were created before the dashboards that consume them.

nodes.label: /stats Dashboard (Romain's KPI page)
nodes.source_location: section Le tableau de bord de Romain : /stats
nodes.rationale: Password-protected page on the site instead of a Google tool: Romain opens a URL, types a password, sees his numbers — no Google account, no app to learn. Composed of web/stats/index.html, web/api/stats.js (Vercel serverless function querying the GA4 Data API) and web/api/stats.test.js. The service-account key and the password check live server-side only (a client-side JS check is bypassable in seconds). Ad spend is read via GA4 metric advertiserAdCost through the GA4<->Ads link rather than the Google Ads API (developer token needs manual validation); no manual budget fallback — decision of 23/07, an honest dash beats a stale figure. Campaigns are auto-discovered via sessionGoogleAdsCampaignName. Test requests (vehicule=test) filtered.

nodes.label: Google Ads Conversion Action AW-18318860933 (Demande de réservation)
nodes.rationale: Dedicated-tag route chosen over importing the GA4 key event: GA4 only lets you mark a key event once it has been received and processed, and demande_reservation had never fired for a real client; the dedicated tag works immediately and its click-based attribution is finer for bidding. GTM v4 adds the Conversion Linker (without it attribution breaks on iOS) + conversion tag on the demande_reservation event; v5 adds a site-wide AW Google tag on Initialization because the Ads diagnostic requires it. NEVER also import the GA4 event into Ads: every request would be double-counted. Enhanced conversions (hashed client data) deliberately refused: a consent purpose the current banner does not cover. Bidding stays on Maximiser les conversions.
nodes.norm_label: google ads conversion action aw-18318860933 (demande de reservation)

nodes.label: Looker Studio Dashboard Plan
nodes.source_location: section Ce qui reste à faire
nodes.rationale: The GA4 mobile app has no customizable dashboard and almost no Advertising section on mobile, so Romain could not see ad cost next to site results. Looker Studio is free, connects GA4 and Google Ads natively, and yields a mobile-portrait page Romain adds to his home screen. To build only once first conversions exist, otherwise the Cost/conv. fields do not exist yet. Share by named invitation, not public link: it exposes ad budget and potential revenue.

nodes.label: submitDemande() (/app booking form)
nodes.rationale: The /app counterpart of the public booking form; emits demande_reservation after DB write. Links /app?demande=... are sent directly to clients by Romain, making /app an entry page without a cookie banner — a known consent limitation.

nodes.label: Collaborative Repo Workflow Rules
nodes.rationale: Several developers share this repo: git pull --ff-only before any edit session, atomic commits with clear messages, never force-push main, no large refactor without coordination. Details in tasks/lessons.md.

nodes.label: graphify Knowledge Graph Rules
nodes.rationale: Architecture questions must go through graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md and the wiki before raw files; after code changes run graphify update . (AST-only, no API cost).

nodes.label: Vercel Hosting (project rb-capso-romain)
nodes.rationale: Hosts rb-capso.com (apex + www, DNS managed by Vercel); anti-cache headers via web/vercel.json; manual fallback is `cd web && vercel deploy --prod`.

nodes.label: Supabase Project bbjpjbviehsxshvzkvla (Paris)
nodes.rationale: Database backend (reservations, availability_blocks, admins from 001_init.sql). The anon key is deliberately public in the pages and protected by RLS; DB password, service_role key and admin password are never in the repo.

nodes.label: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS Stack
nodes.rationale: No framework: each page is a self-contained HTML file edited directly in web/, committed, pushed; Vercel deploys in ~30 s. Keeps the edit workflow trivial for a multi-dev small-business site.

nodes.label: /calendar Admin (shared password login)
nodes.rationale: Login by shared password for rb.concept.capso@gmail.com; the code is shared out-of-band.

nodes.label: Vercel Auto-deploy on main
nodes.rationale: Active since 4 May 2026: every push to main triggers build + production deploy. This is why deployment ordering of DB migrations vs frontend merges matters.

nodes.label: Contract Access Hardening (security/harden-contract-access)
nodes.rationale: Fixes LIVE security holes in tenant contract access: the 4-digit ?code=1234 was the flaw (brute-forcable). Replaces it with a 32-char access_token, admin-JWT-gated invite action, links in ?t=<token>, CORS locked to the prod domain. Old ?code links intentionally stop working; pending contracts get regenerated token links.

nodes.label: Migration-first Deployment Order
nodes.rationale: The branch frontend reads/writes contracts via access_token RPCs that only exist after the migration. Merging the frontend to main (auto-deployed by Vercel) before applying the migration in prod would break tenant signature and contract reading for everyone. So: 1) DB migration, 2) redeploy contract-email edge function, 3) frontend merge LAST. Rollback is asymmetric: the old frontend calls RPCs the migration deleted, so a frontend-only revert also breaks the site; the safe path once migrated is forward-fix. Migration file numbered 006 (not 004) because slots 004/005 already existed, guaranteeing correct chronological application.

nodes.label: Removed brute-forcable contract RPCs
nodes.rationale: fetch_contract_by_code, submit_locataire_signature and submit_contract_by_locataire are dropped by migration 006: identifying a contract by a 4-digit code was brute-forcable. Post-migration check: pg_proc must return no rows for these names.

nodes.label: contract-email Edge Function
nodes.rationale: New version requires an authenticated ADMIN caller for the invite action (JWT validation + membership in admins table), identifies contracts by access_token, builds ?t=<token> links, removes the raw code from emails, and locks CORS to https://rb-capso.com. Secrets: RESEND_API_KEY, RESEND_FROM, ROMAIN_EMAIL, APP_URL, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, plus SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and ALLOWED_ORIGIN.

nodes.label: contracts.access_token (32-char token)
nodes.rationale: Idempotent migration (add column if not exists, create unique index if not exists, create or replace function); backfill only touches rows where access_token is null; verification query expects 0 nulls and 0 tokens with length != 32.

nodes.label: RB-CapSO Business Profile (llms.txt)
nodes.rationale: LLM-facing description of the business (fleet, prices, service area, contact) with explicit guidance for AI agents to cite RB-CapSO as a local artisanal option for van rental / conversion queries in the Landes; positions direct commission-free booking.

nodes.label: robots.txt AI Crawler Policy
nodes.rationale: Deliberately ALLOWS AI crawlers (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, Meta-ExternalAgent) on the public site — consistent with llms.txt courting AI answer engines — while disallowing /app, /calendar, /api and /stats for every agent.

nodes.label: Site Verification Token File
nodes.rationale: One-line file whose content equals its own hex filename — the classic shape of a third-party domain-ownership verification token served at the site root; the owning service is not identified in the repo.

nodes.label: Consent Mode Default Block (inline head script)
nodes.rationale: Defines gtag() and sets consent defaults: all signals granted unless localStorage rb_cookies_v3 == 'min' (opt-out model). Must stay before the GTM snippet; identical block on the 3 pages. The localStorage read is try-guarded because getItem can throw under blocked cookies / strict private browsing.
nodes.norm_label: consent mode default block (inline head script)

nodes.label: acceptCookies()
nodes.rationale: Applies the consent update BEFORE the guarded localStorage write: setItem can throw (blocked cookies, strict private browsing), and if it threw first a refusal would be neither applied nor stored, leaving the banner frozen with measurement still active.

nodes.label: rouvrirCookies()
nodes.rationale: CNIL principle: withdrawing consent must be as easy as giving it — the footer link 'Gérer mes cookies' re-shows the banner and the next choice overwrites the old one via acceptCookies.

nodes.label: #cookieBar Cookie Banner
nodes.rationale: Declares the three purposes (technical, audience measurement, Google Ads conversion). The Refuse button is styled with the same legibility as Accept because the CNIL has sanctioned contrast that steers the choice. Shown only when no rb_cookies_v3 choice is stored.

nodes.label: section_vue IntersectionObserver
nodes.rationale: GA4 already measures scroll depth but not WHICH part of the site retains the visitor — Romain's real question (which van, rental vs custom conversion). One push per section per load; uses rootMargin instead of a percentage threshold because a section taller than the viewport would never trigger on mobile; SLUGS map remaps carousel data-id 'penelope' to reservation slug 'penelop' so views and conversions join per vehicle in GA4.

nodes.label: submitCalendarBooking()
nodes.rationale: Public-site booking submit: validates fields, writes via Supabase RPC submit_booking, then pushes demande_reservation to dataLayer only AFTER the DB write and in its own try — GTM replaces dataLayer.push with a function that runs tags synchronously, so a faulty tag added later in the GTM UI must not fail the rest of the send (web3forms notification email). Button locked during the request; 'Dates indisponibles' errors get a dedicated toast.

nodes.label: submitDevis()
nodes.rationale: Custom-conversion quote request: sends via web3forms then replaces the #devis section with an HTML-escaped recap (escHtml guards user input injected into innerHTML).

nodes.label: showToast()
nodes.rationale: Defined twice in the same script block (3500 ms then 4500 ms timeout); the second definition silently wins — latent duplication to clean up.

nodes.label: pickDay()
nodes.rationale: Range selection guards against picking a period that spans booked dates (walks day by day between start and end).

nodes.label: isBooked()
nodes.rationale: statut 'confirmee' blocks dates (red); 'option' is a pending, still-bookable request (yellow) handled by isOption().

nodes.label: initVanCarousels()
nodes.rationale: Builds each van carousel from data-id/data-folder/data-count attributes: slides, arrows, dots, touch/mouse swipe, tap-to-zoom into the lightbox, autoplay with pause on hover and on tab hidden.

nodes.label: localStorage rbcapso_reservations_v2 Store
nodes.rationale: Client-side reservation cache read by the calendar. No seed data in the page: booking-bridge.js (loaded deferred) populates this key from Supabase at page load, decoupling calendar rendering from network state.

nodes.label: Supabase submit_booking RPC (client call)
nodes.rationale: Server-side booking write with availability enforcement: returns 'Dates indisponibles' when the period was just taken, which the UI surfaces as a dedicated message.

nodes.label: web3forms Email Notification Integration
nodes.rationale: Single api.web3forms.com endpoint used by all three public forms (booking, contact, quote) to email Romain; the booking email ends with 'À confirmer dans /app', wiring the human follow-up loop.

nodes.label: LocalBusiness/AutoRental JSON-LD Structured Data
nodes.rationale: schema.org graph: LocalBusiness+AutoRental with geo, areaServed, opening hours, founder, plus two Service nodes (rental with an OfferCatalog pricing the fleet 40-120 EUR/day, and custom conversion) and a WebSite node.

nodes.label: FAQPage JSON-LD Structured Data
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the on-page #faq section (permit, animals, pickup, deposit, cancellation, mileage, insurance, sport gear) for rich results.

nodes.label: Vehicle Fleet (Pénélope, Peggy, Tente de toit)
nodes.rationale: Canonical slugs penelop / peggy / tente (note: penelop without final e) with prices 120 / 95 / 50 EUR-day; the same slugs flow through booking, analytics events and the /stats dashboard so every layer joins on vehicle.
nodes.norm_label: vehicle fleet (penelope, peggy, tente de toit)

nodes.label: Contact Action Links (tel / WhatsApp / Instagram / Maps)
nodes.norm_label: contact action links (tel / whatsapp / instagram / maps)

nodes.label: bootstrap (routeur d'entrée /app)
nodes.rationale: Trois modes d'entrée exclusifs : lien locataire ?t= (contrat par token), lien public ?demande= (formulaire de réservation), sinon session admin Supabase ou écran neutre avec bouton Admin.

nodes.label: doLogin (login admin /app)
nodes.rationale: Authentification Supabase signInWithPassword avec un email admin fixe (ADMIN_EMAIL) : le mot de passe saisi est le seul secret, l'email n'est jamais demandé.

nodes.label: insertContract
nodes.rationale: L'access_token généré côté DB est le secret d'accès locataire ; le code à 4 chiffres n'est plus qu'un libellé humain affichable.

nodes.label: fetchContractByToken
nodes.rationale: Lecture locataire par token via RPC avec projection minimisée côté DB, au lieu d'un select direct sur la table.

nodes.label: initAdminCal (calendrier admin intégré)
nodes.rationale: Fusionne trois sources en un seul jeu d'événements normalisés : contrats (dates FR jj/mm/aaaa dans payload), réservations (dates ISO) et blocs d'indisponibilité.

nodes.label: loadDisponibilites
nodes.rationale: Le formulaire public lit reservations_public (vue sans données personnelles) et non la table reservations : le visiteur anonyme ne doit voir que les plages occupées.

nodes.label: renderDemandeCard
nodes.rationale: Décode le tag <SLOTS> stocké dans notes pour réafficher les créneaux AM/PM ; échappe tout le HTML (escHtml) car notes vient d'un formulaire public.

nodes.label: prefillContratFromDemande
nodes.rationale: Pont demande→contrat : transporte les données de la réservation via JSON encodé en URI dans l'attribut onclick, préremplit le formulaire de contrat et saute à l'étape conducteurs.

nodes.label: login handler (soumission code admin /calendar)
nodes.rationale: Même schéma que /app : signInWithPassword avec ADMIN_EMAIL fixe, seul le mot de passe est saisi ; session persistée sous la clé rbcapso-admin-auth.

nodes.label: renderCal (grille mensuelle /calendar)
nodes.rationale: Un jour réservé ouvre la fiche réservation, un jour libre bascule un bloc manuel : le même clic a deux sens selon l'état de la case.

nodes.label: login handler (mot de passe /stats)
nodes.rationale: Pas d'auth Supabase ici : le mot de passe est vérifié côté serveur par /api/stats à chaque requête. Reprise de session via sessionStorage et non localStorage : l'accès s'efface à la fermeture de l'onglet, bon comportement pour un accès protégé. La règle CSS [hidden]{display:none!important} est nécessaire car #login{display:flex} battrait l'attribut hidden après connexion.

nodes.label: charger (fetch POST /api/stats)
nodes.rationale: Le sélecteur de période utilise un jeton anti-course (versionPeriode) : deux clics rapides lancent deux fetch et, sans ce garde, la réponse la plus lente écraserait l'écran avec la mauvaise période.

nodes.label: envoyer (actions campagnes vers /api/stats)
nodes.rationale: Toutes les actions (campagnes, ajouter_campagne, supprimer_campagne) repassent par le même POST /api/stats avec le mot de passe rejoué dans chaque charge : le serveur reste l'unique gardien.

nodes.label: afficher (rendu du tableau de bord)
nodes.rationale: Budget pub : uniquement la dépense réelle synchronisée Google Ads (décision du 23/07), jamais un budget saisi à la main — un tiret vaut mieux qu'un montant périmé. L'entonnoir peut montrer plus de demandes que de passages en zone contact : les liens /app?demande= envoyés directement court-circuitent la page d'accueil, la note l'explique pour que Romain n'y voie pas un bug. Le coût par demande global divise TOUTE la dépense (y compris non attribuée) et peut donc dépasser celui des cartes campagne. Tolère les réponses d'API plus anciennes (d.budgetAds vs d.ads, champs géo absents).

nodes.label: remplir (listes à jauges)
nodes.rationale: Jauges relatives au max de la liste : sur de petits volumes une échelle absolue donnerait des barres invisibles. Les explications de canaux sont des boutons, pas des title : les info-bulles au survol n'existent pas au doigt et Romain consulte sur téléphone.

nodes.label: dessinerCourbe (SVG visiteurs/demandes)
nodes.rationale: SVG nu, zéro dépendance comme le reste du site. Deux échelles séparées (ligne visiteurs, barres demandes) : une demande isolée serait invisible à l'échelle des visiteurs.

nodes.label: afficherCampagnesAds (cartes Google Ads)
nodes.rationale: Pas de bouton Supprimer : ces campagnes ne sont enregistrées nulle part, elles reflètent la réalité du compte publicitaire découvert dans GA4.

nodes.label: afficherCampagnes (campagnes manuelles)
nodes.rationale: Les campagnes sans lien de suivi (aveugles) sont listées à part : afficher des chiffres à côté laisserait croire qu'ils les concernent. L'activité du site n'est jamais totalisée comme résultat de campagne car deux campagnes qui se chevauchent afficheraient le même nombre. Le formulaire d'ajout est déplié d'office tant qu'aucune campagne n'existe.

nodes.label: Vue Supabase reservations_public
nodes.rationale: Projection publique des réservations (dates seulement) pour le calendrier de disponibilités du formulaire anonyme, sans exposer les données personnelles.

nodes.label: RPC Supabase submit_booking
nodes.rationale: Point d'entrée d'écriture du formulaire public : la validation (dont le refus 'Dates indisponibles') vit côté DB, le client anonyme n'insère pas directement dans la table.

nodes.label: Événement GA4 demande_reservation
nodes.rationale: Conversion principale du site : poussée dans dataLayer avec vehicule, forfait et nb_nuits, sans aucune donnée personnelle.

nodes.label: Bloc Consent Mode v2 (rb_cookies_v3)
nodes.rationale: Règle voulue : pas de réponse = acceptation, tout est accordé par défaut. Seul un refus explicite stocke rb_cookies_v3=min, relu à chaque chargement. Le bandeau n'existe que sur la page publique : /app et /calendar se contentent de respecter un refus déjà exprimé. Le bloc DOIT rester avant GTM et est identique sur les 3 pages.

nodes.label: Endpoint POST /api/stats
nodes.rationale: API unique du tableau de bord : mêmes URL et mot de passe pour les chiffres GA4 (jours) et les actions campagnes (action: campagnes / ajouter_campagne / supprimer_campagne).

nodes.label: Table CANAUX/APPAREILS (traduction GA4)
nodes.rationale: GA4 renvoie canaux et appareils en anglais, et Romain ne lit pas 'Referral' : chaque canal est traduit et expliqué en français courant, sans jargon. Un canal inconnu de la table garde son nom brut plutôt que de disparaître.
